availability.note: Leapmotor AU B03X page lists Style and Design LR, 'Available to Pre-Order at your Local Dealer Today', with a drive-away offer for cars 'purchased and delivered between 1 October and 31 December'; offers page (https://www.leapmotor.net/en-au/offers) repeats it. Leapmotor AU has no public configurator with prices (same as leapmotor-b10). Buyer's guide dated October 2026 lists both grades. Treated as orderable via dealer pre-order with deliveries promised by 31 Dec 2026; first deliveries not independently confirmed.

listPrice.note: CarExpert (10 Oct 2026): Style 'priced from $26,990 before on-road costs'; EV Central (7 Oct 2026, https://evcentral.com.au/australia-has-a-new-electric-suv-pricing-benchmark-leapmotor-b03x-arrives-from-29990-drive-away/) same before-on-roads figure. Leapmotor itself publishes only the drive-away offer ($29,990 for Style, Acorn Brown, to 31 Dec 2026). Direction check: calc/onroad.js Victorian drive-away for $26,990 is $29,082; the national $29,990 offer sits $908 above it (it bundles 12 months rego, CTP and dealer delivery), and the gap is ~$3,000 above list on both grades, consistent with a genuine list price rather than a discount.

batteryKwh.note: usable per EV Database; nominal 39.8 kWh is the unlabelled figure in Leapmotor AU buyer's guide (https://www.leapmotor.net/docs/lpmiwebsiteenaulibraries/brochures/b03x-buyers-guide-2026.pdf). LFP; same pack sizes as the European B03X.

rangeKm.note: Leapmotor AU buyer's guide (Oct 2026): EV range up to 292 km (WLTP). No NEDC figure published. Both grades on 18-inch wheels (18-inch steel), the only wheel offered per grade, so the 'up to' figure is the local car. EV Database gives the same WLTP figure.

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: Leapmotor AU buyer's guide: energy consumption 155 Wh/km WLTP (includes charging losses). batteryKwh/rangeKm gives 13.4, within the 25% cross-check.

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: Leapmotor AU buyer's guide: rear cargo volume behind 2nd row 475 L; measurement method not stated. Reviews quote Leapmotor's international 510 L including a 105 L underfloor bin (CarExpert review), and EV Database gives 407 L (European). 475 L is the Australian manufacturer figure and its 1,315 L folded figure is well below the 1,605 L international (likely to-roof) figure, suggesting a to-the-cover/belt-line basis. No frunk.

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: Leapmotor AU buyer's guide: behind 1st row 1,315 L. International/review figure 1,605 L not used (likely to roof).

seats.note: EV Database: 5 seats; AU buyer's guide shows a 60/40 rear bench with ISOFIX.

towKg.note: CarExpert review: not homologated for towing at launch; towbar and rating planned for a future model year. AU buyer's guide and CarExpert towing page list no capacity; EV Database lists 0 kg.

warrantyYears.note: Leapmotor AU buyer's guide: vehicle warranty 6 years/150,000 km; HV battery 8 years/160,000 km. Unconditional. CarExpert price article agrees.

insuranceAnnual.note: anchored to mg-4-urban-43 ($29,780, $1,250), byd-atto1-premium ($27,990, $1,200), byd-dolphin-essential ($29,990, $1,250) and geely-ex2-complete ($26,490, $1,150); leapmotor-b10-style sits ~$50 above BYD peers, so Leapmotor small-brand loading kept

depreciationCurve.note: Leapmotor brand curve [1, 0.72, 0.59, 0.5, 0.43, 0.37] as held on leapmotor-b10 and leapmotor-c10, per dispatcher and the one-curve-per-brand convention.
